raw.body:
React version: 19.2.6

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Open the repro repository: https://github.com/andyzhan7/react-suspense-fallback-throttle

2. Open either reproduction file:
   - `precreated-routes.html`
   - `render-created-loader.html`

3. Wait until the `Student` and `Teacher` loaders have been preloaded.

4. Click `Student` or `Teacher`.

Link to code example: https://github.com/andyzhan7/react-suspense-fallback-throttle

## The current behavior

A route component loaded through `React.lazy` can be delayed by about 300ms on its first render, even when the loader promise has already resolved before that render.

The repro uses this minimal lazy route wrapper:

```js
function LazyLoader(loader) {
  const Comp = React.lazy(loader)
  return props => React.createElement(
    React.Suspense,
    null,
    React.createElement(Comp, props || null),
  )
}
```

The route loaders are preloaded on page load. They simulate network/chunk loading with a short `sleep(...)`, so by the time the user clicks `Student` or `Teacher`, the loader promise has already resolved.

However, the first render of the lazy route still commits about 300ms later:

```text
0.5ms loader called: Student
302.1ms content committed: Student
```

Because the Suspense boundary has no fallback, this appears as a blank content area for about 300ms.

## The expected behavior

If a `React.lazy` loader promise has already resolved, React should render the loaded component as soon as that resolved promise is observed, instead of waiting for the 300ms fallback throttle window.

In this case, after clicking `Student` or `Teacher`, the route content should commit immediately or near-immediately because the lazy loader promise was already resolved by preload.
raw.title: Bug: React.lazy waits ~300ms before rendering even when the preloaded promise has resolved
